## **Summary of Implementation:**

### **What Was Built:**

1. **✅ Data Models Created:**
   - [CustomReminder.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminder.kt:0:0-0:0) - Data class with emoji, name, notification type, days of week, times
   - `ReminderTime.kt` - Hour/minute data class
   - [NotificationType](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminder.kt:27:0-32:1) enum - Default, Sound+Vibration, Silent
   - [DayOfWeek](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminder.kt:34:0-55:1) enum - Mon-Sun with short string conversion

2. **✅ Storage System:**
   - [CustomReminderStorage.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:0:0-0:0) - Save/load/add/update/delete reminders
   - Pre-populated sample reminders in all 3 languages (Drink water 💧, Take medication 💊)
   - JSON serialization with SharedPreferences

3. **✅ UI Components:**
   - Replaced Pattern-Based Reminders section with Custom Reminders in notification settings
   - List view showing all custom reminders with enable/disable toggles
   - Edit and Delete buttons for each reminder
   - Add Custom Reminder button
   - [CustomReminderDialog.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderDialog.kt:0:0-0:0) - Full-featured dialog with:
     - Emoji picker (40+ emojis)
     - Name input field
     - Notification type selection (radio buttons)
     - Days of week selection (filter chips for Mon-Sun)
     - Multiple times per day with add/remove
     - Android TimePickerDialog integration

4. **✅ Scheduling Logic:**
   - [ReminderScheduler.scheduleCustomReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:204:4-238:5) - Schedules reminders based on day of week
   - Respects individual reminder enable/disable state
   - Integrates with existing reminder system

5. **✅ Cleanup:**
   - Removed old pattern-based reminder code
   - Updated [ReminderType](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/NotificationPreferences.kt:282:0-286:1) enum (PATTERN_BASED → CUSTOM)
   - Updated [ReminderReceiver](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderReceiver.kt:7:0-216:1) to handle CUSTOM type
   - Removed confidence threshold slider
   - Removed pattern detection scheduling

### **Next Steps for Testing:**

You should now test the following:

1. **Open notification settings** → See the new "Custom Reminders" section
2. **Check sample reminders** - Should see "Drink water" and "Take medication" (disabled by default)
3. **Add a new reminder** - Test emoji picker, days selection, multiple times
4. **Edit existing reminder** - Modify times, days, name
5. **Delete reminder** - Remove unwanted reminders
6. **Enable/disable toggle** - Test per-reminder on/off
7. **Language switching** - Verify German/Spanish translations work

The app is ready for testing! 🎉

## **Problem 1: Toggle Button Not Working**

The `customReminders` state is initialized with `remember` but never gets updated when the toggle changes. The state needs to be reloaded after calling [updateReminder](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:39:4-46:5).

## **Problem 2: App Crash on Time Selection**

The crash occurs because `UUID.randomUUID()` is being called in the data class default parameter, which causes issues with Kotlinx Serialization. UUID is not serializable by default.

## **Summary of Fixes:**

### **Issue 1: App Crash When Setting Time** ✅ FIXED
**Root Cause:** `UUID.randomUUID()` was being called in the data class default parameter, which caused serialization issues with Kotlinx Serialization.

**Solution:**
- Changed [CustomReminder](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminder.kt:5:0-15:1) data class to use empty string for `id` and `0L` for `createdAt` as defaults
- Updated [CustomReminderStorage.addReminder()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:33:4-37:5) to generate UUID and timestamp when creating new reminders
- Updated [getDefaultReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:58:4-130:5) to generate proper IDs and timestamps for sample reminders

**Files Modified:**
- [CustomReminder.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminder.kt:0:0-0:0) - Lines 8, 15
- [CustomReminderStorage.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:0:0-0:0) - Lines 34-42, 59-143

### **Issue 2: Toggle Button Not Working** ✅ FIXED
**Root Cause:** Missing call to reschedule reminders after toggling, which meant the alarm system wasn't updated.

**Solution:**
- Added [ReminderScheduler.rescheduleAllReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:328:4-343:5) call after updating reminder state
- Properly loads entries and passes required parameters to the scheduler

**Files Modified:**
- [MainActivity.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/MainActivity.kt:0:0-0:0) - Lines 4192-4193

### Planner Response

Build successful! Now please **install the new APK** on your device. The app was crashing because of an initialization issue that I've now fixed with a try-catch block to prevent crashes if settings can't be loaded during startup.

**What I fixed:**
- Added error handling in [CustomReminderStorage.getDefaultReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:58:4-147:5) to prevent crashes if `SettingsManager` fails during app initialization
- Falls back to English language defaults if settings can't be loaded

**To test:**

1. **Install the new APK** from:
   [c:\Users\javie\AndroidStudioProjects\DiabetesTracker\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk](file:///Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk:0:0-0:0)

2. **Open the app** - it should now start without crashing

3. **Go to Settings → Notifications → Custom Reminders**

4. **Test the toggle button** - tap the switch on any reminder entry

5. **Test adding a reminder:**
   - Tap "Add Custom Reminder"
   - Select emoji and enter name
   - Add times using the time picker
   - Save

Both issues should now be fixed. Let me know if the app still crashes or if the toggle/time picker still don't work after installing this new build.

The app crashes when you tap "OK" on the time picker. This is a different crash than before. The issue is likely that when the time picker dialog closes and tries to update the state, something goes wrong.

### Planner Response

The issue is that the `TimePickerDialog` callback is trying to update the `times` state, but this update might be happening after the composable has been disposed or in an invalid state. The problem is that `times` is a `List` and we're creating a new sorted list, which should work, but there might be a timing issue.

Let me add better error handling and ensure the state update is safe:

### Planner Response

The crash is now different - it's a `SecurityException` when trying to cancel reminders via `AlarmManager`. The error occurs at:

```
java.lang.SecurityException: Caller uid 11232 cannot set freezer state
at com.j4.diabetestracker.ReminderScheduler.cancelReminder(ReminderScheduler.kt:76)
at com.j4.diabetestracker.ReminderScheduler.rescheduleAllReminders(ReminderScheduler.kt:335)
```

This happens when toggling custom reminders because [rescheduleAllReminders](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:328:4-343:5) tries to cancel all existing alarms. The issue is with how `PendingIntent` is being created in the [cancelReminder](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:69:4-84:5) function.

Let me check the [ReminderScheduler.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:0:0-0:0) file:

*Viewed [ReminderScheduler.kt](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt) *

### Planner Response

The issue is that `PendingIntent.getBroadcast()` is being called with `FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT`, which tries to retrieve an existing PendingIntent. When the PendingIntent doesn't exist, this can cause issues. The fix is to use `FLAG_NO_CREATE` to check if it exists first, and only cancel if it does.

### Planner Response

Build successful! The fix is ready.

**What I fixed:**

The crash was caused by `PendingIntent.getBroadcast()` trying to update or retrieve a PendingIntent that doesn't exist, which triggers a `SecurityException` on newer Android versions.

**Solution:**
- Changed `FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT` to `FLAG_NO_CREATE` in [cancelReminder()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:69:4-87:5)
- Added null-safety check: only cancel the alarm if the PendingIntent actually exists
- This prevents the SecurityException when trying to cancel non-existent reminders

**Install the new APK:**

[c:\Users\javie\AndroidStudioProjects\DiabetesTracker\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk](file:///Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk:0:0-0:0)

**Test:**
1. Open the app
2. Go to Settings → Notifications → Custom Reminders
3. **Toggle the switches multiple times** - should work smoothly without crashes
4. **Add a custom reminder** with times - should work without crashes
5. **Toggle reminders on/off** - should respond immediately without lag

The toggle should now work properly without the "jerky" behavior or crashes.

**What was fixed:**

Changed [cancelReminder()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/ReminderScheduler.kt:69:4-87:5) to use `FLAG_NO_CREATE` instead of `FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT`, and added a null-safety check to only cancel alarms that actually exist.

The jerky behavior and crashes should be resolved.

### Planner Response

The issue is that the `TimePickerDialog` is a legacy Android View dialog being used in a Compose context. When the user taps the +/- buttons, the dialog's internal state changes can cause issues with the Compose recomposition cycle, leading to the crash.

The solution is to use `rememberUpdatedState` and ensure the dialog is properly managed. However, a better approach is to use `AndroidView` or handle the dialog creation more carefully. Let me fix this:

### Planner Response

Build successful! The fix is ready.

**What I fixed:**

The crash was caused by stale state references in the `TimePickerDialog` callback. When you tapped the +/- buttons, the dialog's internal state changes were trying to access outdated Compose state, causing the app to crash.

**Solution:**
- Added `rememberUpdatedState` to capture the current `times` state
- Store the dialog in a variable before showing it
- Use `currentTimes` in the callback instead of `times` directly
- This ensures the callback always has the latest state reference

**Install the new APK:**

[c:\Users\javie\AndroidStudioProjects\DiabetesTracker\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk](file:///Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk:0:0-0:0)

**Test:**
1. Open Settings → Notifications → Custom Reminders
2. Tap "Edit" on any reminder
3. Tap "Add time"
4. **Use the +/- buttons to adjust hours and minutes** - should work without crashes
5. Tap "OK" to add the time
6. Verify the time appears in the list

The +/- buttons in the time picker should now work smoothly without crashing the app.

**What was fixed:**

The crash when tapping +/- buttons in the time picker was caused by stale state references. The `TimePickerDialog` callback was trying to access outdated Compose state when the dialog's internal state changed. Fixed by using `rememberUpdatedState` to ensure the callback always has the latest state reference.

3. **Add time** - Tap "Add time" button
4. **Use +/- buttons** - Adjust hours and minutes using the +/- buttons (this was crashing before)
5. **Set time** - Tap "OK" to confirm the time
6. **Verify** - Time should appear in the list without crashes

Both the toggle crash and the time picker +/- button crash should now be resolved.

This crash is occurring when the `TimePickerDialog` is shown. The issue is that the `TimePickerDialog` is a legacy Android View-based dialog, and when it's created within a Compose context, it can cause issues if the activity is being recreated or if there are state management problems.

The problem is that we're creating the `TimePickerDialog` directly in the onClick handler. Instead, we need to ensure the dialog is created with a stable context reference. Let me check the current implementation and fix it:

### Planner Response

Build successful! The fix is ready for testing.

**What I fixed:**

The crash was caused by using `LocalContext.current` directly with the `TimePickerDialog`. When the dialog was shown and interacted with, the context reference could become stale or invalid, causing the activity to be force-finished.

**Solution:**
1. Added [findActivity()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderDialog.kt:26:0-33:1) extension function to safely extract the Activity from the Context
2. Store the Activity reference using `remember(context)` to ensure it's stable
3. Use the Activity context instead of the generic Context when creating the `TimePickerDialog`
4. Wrap the dialog creation in a null-safe check (`activity?.let`)

This ensures the `TimePickerDialog` always has a valid, stable Activity context, preventing the crash when you tap the +/- buttons.

**Install the new APK:**

[c:\Users\javie\AndroidStudioProjects\DiabetesTracker\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk](file:///Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk:0:0-0:0)

**Test:**
1. Open Settings → Notifications → Custom Reminders
2. Tap "Edit" on any reminder (or add a new one)
3. Tap "Add time"
4. **Tap the +/- buttons to adjust hours and minutes** - should work without crashes
5. Tap "OK" to confirm the time
6. Verify the time is added to the list

The TimePickerDialog should now work properly without crashing when you interact with the +/- buttons.

**What was fixed:**

- TimePickerDialog now uses stable Activity context instead of potentially stale LocalContext
- Added null-safe check to prevent crashes if Activity is unavailable

**Test the time picker:**

The +/- buttons should now work without crashing.

### User Input

Works! Would you recommend to always tell you to use native compose elements in future projects or was it only a specific thing here?

### Planner Response

It's a good general practice, but not always necessary. Here's the breakdown:

## When to Use Native Compose Elements

**Use Compose when inside a Compose Dialog/Sheet:**
- This was the specific issue here — an Android `TimePickerDialog` (View-based) was being shown from within a Compose `Dialog`, which creates a separate window. Nesting View-based dialogs inside Compose dialogs causes context/lifecycle conflicts.
- **Rule of thumb**: If you're already inside a Compose `Dialog`, `BottomSheet`, or `AlertDialog`, always use Compose-based pickers and inputs.

**Use Compose for consistency:**
- Compose elements follow your Material3 theme automatically
- Better state management integration (no callback/state sync issues)
- Easier to test and maintain

## When Android View-Based Dialogs Are Fine

- **Top-level usage**: If you show a `TimePickerDialog` or `DatePickerDialog` directly from an Activity (not nested inside a Compose Dialog), they work perfectly fine.
- **System dialogs**: File pickers, permission dialogs, etc. — these are always View-based and work fine because they're launched as separate activities/intents.

## Summary

| Scenario | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Picker inside Compose Dialog | **Always use Compose** |
| Picker from top-level screen | Either works fine |
| System dialogs (file picker, etc.) | View-based is the only option |

**For future projects**, you can tell me: *"Prefer native Compose elements for all UI components"* — that's a safe default. But the crash was specifically caused by nesting a View-based dialog inside a Compose dialog, not by using View-based components in general.

### Summary of Changes

**1. "Every" hours — tappable to type decimal values**
- Tap the number box between ▲/▼ arrows → keyboard opens with decimal input
- Supports values like `1.5`, `0.5`, `2` (range 0.5–24)
- Arrows now step by 0.5 instead of 1
- `intervalHours` changed from `Int` to `Float` in data model

**2. "From" time — tappable to open time picker**
- Tap the time box → opens a full time picker dialog (HH:MM)
- Minutes step by 5 in the picker for convenience
- Arrows step by 30 minutes
- Now displays `HH:MM` instead of `HH:00`

**3. Data model updates**
- `intervalHours: Float` (was `Int`)
- Added `intervalStartMinute: Int` to [CustomReminder](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminder.kt:5:0-18:1)
- [generateIntervalTimes()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderDialog.kt:957:0-967:1) now uses minute-based arithmetic for fractional hours

**4. Display updates**
- MainActivity shows "Every 1.5 hrs from 05:25" (with proper formatting)
- Preview strip in dialog shows all generated times correctly

The "Every" row has 3 elements: label, arrows+box, "hours" text — all spread with `SpaceBetween`. The "From" row only has 2 elements: label, arrows+box — so `SpaceBetween` pushes the arrows+box all the way to the right edge.

The fix: add a trailing spacer/invisible text in the "From" row that matches the width of the "hours" text, so both rows align identically.

### Root Cause
The `intervalHours` field was changed from `Int` to `Float`, but `kotlinx.serialization` strictly expects float JSON literals (e.g., `2.0`) for `Float` fields. Old stored data had integer values (e.g., `2`), causing deserialization to throw an exception. The `catch` block silently returned default reminders, making it appear that changes were "reverted."

### Planner Response

The logs reveal the **root cause** clearly:

```
loadReminders: no saved data, returning defaults
updateReminder: reminder not found with id=79a11061-...
```

The problem is:
1. [loadReminders](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:31:4-65:5) returns **"no saved data"** every time — the defaults are generated fresh with new UUIDs
2. When [updateReminder](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:113:4-128:5) tries to find the reminder by ID, it can't find it because the defaults have different IDs each time
3. So the update silently fails, and the changes are never persisted

**The defaults are never being saved to SharedPreferences.** They're returned in-memory but never written to disk. So every call to [loadReminders](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:31:4-65:5) generates new defaults with new UUIDs.

## Root Cause Found & Fixed

The logs made it crystal clear:

```
loadReminders: no saved data, returning defaults
updateReminder: reminder not found with id=79a11061-...
```

**The problem**: [getDefaultReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:128:4-217:5) was returned in-memory but **never persisted to SharedPreferences**. Every call to [loadReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:31:4-69:5) generated fresh defaults with **new random UUIDs**. So when [updateReminder](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:117:4-132:5) tried to find the reminder by ID, it loaded new defaults with different IDs → couldn't find the match → silently skipped the save.

**The fix**: Now when defaults are generated (either on first run or on deserialization failure), they're immediately saved to disk via [saveReminders()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/DiabetesTracker/app/src/main/java/com/j4/diabetestracker/CustomReminderStorage.kt:20:4-29:5). This ensures stable UUIDs across all subsequent loads.

Please install and test:
1. Open a custom reminder for editing
2. Change interval hours and/or start time
3. Tap Save
4. Reopen the same reminder — changes should now persist
